findings.claim: `self.downsize` is defined twice in OptimizedImage. Ruby has no overloading, so the later (from, to, dimensions, opts) definition replaces the (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) one, and existing 5-argument callers such as ResizeEmoji (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) raise ArgumentError.

API URL-based uploads now call FileHelper.download with a hardcoded 10.megabytes cap instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. This ignores the configured limit: larger files are truncated or blocked on sites allowing more than 10 MB, and more than allowed is downloaded on sites with smaller limits.

Client-side upload validation hardcodes maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 for all upload types instead of using Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. Files the server will reject can pass the browser check, and files that sites configured above 10 MB allow are blocked.
The same 10 MB constant is duplicated in several places, so the client and server limits can drift apart.
The HTTP 413 handler always reports a limit of 10240 KB, although the actual limit depends on the nginx/proxy client_max_body_size setting.
The error message in displayErrorForUpload (line 246) shows a hardcoded 10 MB instead of the actual configured limit when the server rejects a file for exceeding a smaller configured limit.
In the switch statement, `case 413` declares `maxSizeKB` without a surrounding block, so the declaration is visible to the other cases.

The downsize loop reads `tempfile.size`, which stays stale after the in-place downsize and ImageOptim rename. As a result, the loop may run all passes or fail to terminate correctly, and Upload.create_for receives a stale filesize, dimensions and a mismatched sha1.
Downsizing passes '80%' as the dimensions. For animated GIFs this goes to `gifsicle --resize-fit`, which accepts only WxH pixel geometry, so gifsicle fails and every retry attempt is used up.
The allow_animation option is effectively dead code, because animated GIF downsizing fails through both upload paths.
Each upload can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick plus ImageOptim runs on files up to 10 MB.
When OptimizedImage.downsize fails and returns false, the loop ignores the result, keeps retrying, and lets the oversized file continue.
The downsize loop shrinks the image to only about 33% of the original after 5 iterations (0.8^5), so an image can still exceed max_image_size_kb and proceed to Upload.create_for.
Non-API uploads run in the shared Scheduler::Defer.later queue, so large uploads stall unrelated deferred work.
No tests cover the new downsize loop, the changed OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize signatures, or the client validation change.
Image processing uses the same path for input and output, so the original file is lost if the operation fails mid-write.
With allow_animated_thumbnails off, `convert file[0]` writes only the first frame back over the original GIF.
For regular browser uploads, Rack tempfile paths lack a .gif extension, so the GIF detection regex in optimize() never matches and `convert` with [0] strips animation from GIFs.
The `tempfile &&` and `tempfile.size > 0` checks in the new guard are redundant with the loop condition and the later handling of a nil tempfile.
FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so oversized SVGs enter the downsize loop and ImageMagick rewrites the user's SVG in place.
An inline `rescue nil` silently swallows all exceptions, including network errors.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
